title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to test whether integrating a deterministic Batfish-style validator and a bounded automated repair iteration reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The sealed preregistration (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) specified 200 paired tasks balanced across four strata (IOS-like vs JunOS-like × single-step vs multi-step), a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), and a bounded generate→validate→repair adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) with ≤1 repair attempt per task under a shared_initial_generation execution contract. All archived artifacts report both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200). The observed absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed archived) and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair count = 0); the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is therefore not computable. We report artifact-backed reconciliations, interpret the degenerate confirmatory outcome, and discuss construct, internal, and external-validity limits and follow-up sensitivity designs.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models promise to accelerate NetOps by translating high-level operator intent into device configuration, but they can introduce deployment risk when generated configurations violate safety or policy constraints (reachability, ACL/policy, routing, or interface-state invariants). A widely proposed mitigation is a generate→validate→repair workflow that places a deterministic verifier (e.g., Batfish) in the loop and optionally issues automated repairs or human approvals. Prior work prototypes such workflows and argues for layered architectural controls, but preregistered paired evidence quantifying the marginal verifier benefit under a strict estimand and bounded repair budget is limited. We therefore asked: Does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors relative to one-shot LLM generation? Contributions: (1) a sealed preregistered paired confirmatory design (n=200) with a single primary estimand and an automated analysis executor; (2) a fully automated execution using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic Batfish-style validator under a shared_initial_generation contract; (3) an artifact-backed degenerate confirmatory outcome (zero discordant pairs) and a focused discussion of implications for design sensitivity and follow-on study dimensions.
sections.related_work: Recent literature demonstrates active interest in LLM-driven NetOps and proposes verifier-in-the-loop patterns, bounded self-correction, and orchestration frameworks. Representative works include Nguyen Tu et al., “Intent‐Based Network Configuration Using Large Language Models” (Networks and Spatial Economics / 2024) documenting intent-to-configuration pipelines; Wei et al., “INTA: Intent-Based Translation for Network Configuration with LLM Agents” (ICNP 2025) describing LLM-driven translation prototypes; Sang, “AutoCrit: A Meta-Reasoning Framework for Self-Critique and Iterative Error Correction in LLM Chains-of-Thought” (ICMLCA 2025) proposing iterative repair/meta-reasoning; Mekrache & Ksentini, “LLM-enabled Intent-driven Service Configuration for Next Generation Networks” (NetSoft 2024) exploring intent-driven service configuration; and Nan, “Z-SPACE: A MULTI-AGENT TOOL ORCHESTRATION FRAMEWORK FOR ENTERPRISE-GRADE LLM AUTOMATION” (2025, reported as a system proposal). Surveys and recent preprints argue for workflow-centred evaluation, verifier fidelity, and layered runtime controls (agent orchestration, traceability, and human gates). These studies motivate generate→validate→repair designs but typically report prototypes or position arguments rather than preregistered paired trials isolating the verifier marginal effect under a fixed repair budget.
sections.methodology: Study design and preregistration: We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate). Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided (α=0.05); uncertainty via paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples). Sampling and strata: 200 paired tasks balanced across four strata (50 tasks each: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step). Model and pipeline: declared model = gpt-5-mini; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 implementing a bounded generate→validate→repair transformation with ≤1 repair attempt per task. Harm oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implemented Batfish-style checks (reachability, ACL/policy, routing-loop detection, interface-state regressions) and applied a full-intent-constraint validation rule to mark validator-detected errors. Crucial preregistered execution contract detail (required revision addressed here): the design used shared_initial_generation (independent_condition_generation = false), i.e., one initial generation candidate per task was produced and reused for both the baseline and guarded condition; this choice intentionally constrains detectable differences to validator-triggered repairs rather than to generator-stochasticity differences (see execution/model_configuration.json and deterministic_reconciliation provider_call_audit). Execution and failure handling: planned episodes = 400 (200 tasks × 2 conditions), maximum_model_calls = 400, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; missingness: complete-pair policy for primary analysis; conservative sensitivity rules preregistered. Analysis: automated executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 computed contingency tables, exact McNemar p-value, and paired-bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples). All prompts, seeds, model traces, validator logs, canonicalized configurations, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.results: Execution and scoring (artifact-backed): planned episodes = 400, completed episodes = 400, failed episodes = 0; provider_call_audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 (consistent with one shared initial generation per task; execution/model_configuration.json and deterministic_reconciliation.json are archived). Condition summaries from analysis/condition_summary.csv: baseline validator-clean = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0); guarded validator-clean = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Estimated paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired-bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples; seed archived) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0 (artifact: analysis/results.json). Repair activity: zero tasks triggered a repair (repair count = 0); therefore the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. Supporting artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/scoring/*.json (representative files under execution/scoring/), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (all archived and cited in the evidence bundle). Representative episode-level scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, etc.) show identical shared-initial, baseline, and guarded responses for sampled tasks and validator traces indicating valid = true and repair_applied = false.
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation: the observed data are degenerate for the paired estimand because there were no discordant pairs; McNemar's p = 1.0 and the degenerate bootstrap CI correctly reflect that outcome. This empirical null does not imply verifier-in-the-loop defenses are universally unnecessary. Several preregistered design choices and task-bank properties limit detectable marginal verifier benefit: (1) shared_initial_generation intentionally suppresses generator-induced discordance—differences between arms could only arise if the guarded pipeline applied repairs after validator detection; (2) the synthetic task corpus is template-aligned and may under-challenge the generator, increasing baseline cleanliness; (3) a single model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair) restrict the range of behaviors examined; (4) deterministic_netops_validator_v5 approximates Batfish semantics in sandbox scenarios but cannot reproduce all vendor-specific production quirks. Operational implication: when generation already produces validator-clean outputs for the chosen task bank and generation variance is suppressed by shared-generation, a bounded single-repair iteration will not yield measurable marginal gains. Recommended follow-ups (consistent with preregistration sensitivity plans): (a) independent_condition_generation (separate model calls per arm) to reintroduce generator variance and detect differences arising from stochastic generation; (b) expand the repair budget to iterative repairs (≥2) and measure repair-success rates; (c) test multiple model families and temperatures; (d) increase task heterogeneity and introduce adversarial/prompt-injection scenarios; (e) evaluate richer verifier environments including device-in-the-loop emulation.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial of a bounded generate→validate→repair workflow (gpt-5-mini + deterministic Batfish-style validator) on 200 synthetic intent-to-configuration tasks. Both arms were validator-clean on every task (200/200), yielding an observed paired difference of 0.0 (95% paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0]) and McNemar p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked; therefore the preregistered repair-success hypothesis could not be evaluated. The null outcome highlights how execution contracts (shared vs independent generation), task difficulty, model choice, and verifier expressiveness jointly determine when verifier-assisted repairs are measurable. We release the preregistration and full execution/analysis artifacts to enable follow-up preregistered studies that vary these dimensions to identify regimes where verifier-assisted repairs yield operational gains.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic, public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-like sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or unbounded-repair claims are made.

Preregistered shared_initial_generation (independent_condition_generation=false) produced one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduces the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items (contamination summary archived), but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
